events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.93)
events.body:
This is a no-show cancellation fee dispute: the driver cancelled at 14:15:50 and $6.61 was charged [F4][F7], so it enters the policy through NS-0's driver-cancelled, no-show-claimed branch [RD-2][NS-0]. The driver's written statement that he "waited for the rider, then cancelled as a no-show" [F12] is a statement, not a system record, and the system records (GPS/timeline) override it [F5][F6].

NS-1 requires all three limbs. The arrival precondition is genuinely met: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 14:14:10 at 41 m from the pickup [F6], matching NS-1(i) and NS-1(ii), and this is confirmed by the trace [F1][NS-1]. The trace also settles the GPS coverage of the wait with no hole [F2][F6][NS-1], so G12 manual referral is not triggered.

The decisive limb, NS-1(iii), fails on the trace: continuously inside the 200 m radius after the tap was 100 s, below the >180 s threshold [F6], and the cumulative time within 200 m before cancellation was only 2 min 25 s [F2][F5]. The driver's chat "3 min up, cancelling the trip" [F10] and the 2 min 0 s stationary period at 41 m [F3] do not rescue it. The driver did not tap outside the radius [F6], so no NS-2 fraud flag applies, and the trace marks the flag_account condition ✗ [F1][F6][NS-2].

With NS-1(iii) unsatisfied, NS-2 requires the $6.61 to be refunded in full; the amount follows the trace (cancellation fee $6.61) [F4][F7][NS-2]. The rider's request for refund_full is therefore granted.

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7); no account flag on the driver, as the arrival tap was genuine (41 m).
ruling.reasoning:
This is a no-show cancellation fee dispute: the driver cancelled at 14:15:50 and $6.61 was charged [F4][F7], so it enters the policy through NS-0's driver-cancelled, no-show-claimed branch [RD-2][NS-0]. The driver's written statement that he "waited for the rider, then cancelled as a no-show" [F12] is a statement, not a system record, and the system records (GPS/timeline) override it [F5][F6].

NS-1 requires all three limbs. The arrival precondition is genuinely met: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 14:14:10 at 41 m from the pickup [F6], matching NS-1(i) and NS-1(ii), and this is confirmed by the trace [F1][NS-1]. The trace also settles the GPS coverage of the wait with no hole [F2][F6][NS-1], so G12 manual referral is not triggered.

The decisive limb, NS-1(iii), fails on the trace: continuously inside the 200 m radius after the tap was 100 s, below the >180 s threshold [F6], and the cumulative time within 200 m before cancellation was only 2 min 25 s [F2][F5]. The driver's chat "3 min up, cancelling the trip" [F10] and the 2 min 0 s stationary period at 41 m [F3] do not rescue it. The driver did not tap outside the radius [F6], so no NS-2 fraud flag applies, and the trace marks the flag_account condition ✗ [F1][F6][NS-2].

With NS-1(iii) unsatisfied, NS-2 requires the $6.61 to be refunded in full; the amount follows the trace (cancellation fee $6.61) [F4][F7][NS-2]. The rider's request for refund_full is therefore granted.

rejected_claims.reason: Not rejected as inaccurate but irrelevant to the outcome: the arrival precondition the driver invokes (tap at 41 m) is true [F6][NS-1], yet NS-1 still requires (iii), which the trace fails at 100 s [F6][NS-1].
The driver's own measurement confirms the fee cannot stand: the strictest wait after the tap was 1 min 40 s and the stationary period was 2 min 0 s, both below the NS-1(iii) default [F3][F6][NS-1].
Accepted only in the direction it points: the post-trip statement and chat lose to the system records [F9][F10][F12][F2][F3][F6], which is why the $6.61 fee cannot be sustained under NS-2.

Not disputed as far as it goes — the driver did tap at the pickup and charged no $5 waiting fee [F6][F7] — but this does not validate the $6.61 cancellation fee, which fails NS-1(iii) and falls to NS-2.

Account flag refused: RD-6 applies to upheld route-deviation breaches, not no-show cases, and F17 shows route: 0; NS-2's flag_account requires the arrival tap to have been made outside 200 m, and the tap was at 41 m [F6][F17][NS-2][RD-6].

events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: Good news — your $6.61 cancellation fee is being refunded in full as a Ryde voucher. We checked the trip records: the driver did tap "I'm Here," but the time spent waiting at your pickup point was shorter than our no-show rule requires, so the cancellation fee shouldn't have applied to you. No action is needed on your part, and there's no mark on your account. The voucher will be added to your Ryde account for your next ride.

DRIVER: We reviewed the cancellation of this trip and are refunding the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher. The trip records show you did arrive and tap "I'm Here" near the pickup point, so this isn't treated as a false claim and no flag has been placed on your account. However, the recorded waiting time was below what our no-show rule requires before a fee can be charged. Nothing you need to do — just be aware that a cancellation fee needs that minimum wait time to stand.

what_would_change: Had NS-1 (iii) held ((iii) stayed at the pickup more than 3 min after the arrival confirmation, until cancelling (NS-1 default: more than 3 min)), the fee would stand and no refund would be due.

claims.assertion: The driver's "I'm Here" tap at 14:14:10 was only 41 m from the pickup point, so NS-1(i) and (ii) are satisfied (within the 200 m arrival radius recorded by the system).

After the tap the driver remained within 200 m of the pickup for only 1 min 40 s before cancelling at 14:15:50 (F6), and GPS shows cumulative time within 200 m before cancellation of 2 min 25 s (F2) — both well under the 3 min 01 s continuous-wait requirement, so NS-1(iii) fails and the $6.61 cancellation fee does not stand.

The driver's own chat message at 14:15 claims only "3 min up, cancelling the trip", but the timeline shows cancellation came 1 min 40 s after the tap and the driver was stationary only 14:13:50–14:15:50 (2 min 0 s) at 41 m from the pickup (F3); the claimed waiting time is not supported by the system records.

Platform-recorded arrival was 14:13:25 and the driver cancelled 2 min 25 s later (F5) — within the same short window after acceptance — so no free-wait threshold was ever reached; the $6.61 fee charged (F7) should be refunded in full.

Because the driver pressed "I'm Here" but the requirements for a valid no-show charge were not met, the rider should not bear any part of the $6.61 cancellation fee and no amount is owed under the cancellation policy.

The driver's written statement that he "waited for the rider, then cancelled as a no-show" (F12) is contradicted by the GPS and timeline records of 1 min 40 s of waiting after the tap, so it cannot establish the fee.

The driver has 1 upheld no-show dispute in the last 90 days in addition to this case, which supports an additional account review alongside the refund (profile facts do not by themselves decide the case).

weaknesses: The driver did tap "I'm Here" at 41 m from the pickup (F6), so the arrival precondition NS-1(i)/(ii) is genuinely met — our case rests entirely on the duration limb NS-1(iii) (F2, F5, F6).

The driver was stationary for 2 min 0 s (F3) and the rider never appears in the chat as replying or confirming boarding (F11), so the other side will argue the rider simply did not show up and the wait was long enough.

The driver's chat at 14:15 says "3 min up" (F10); a judge could read the driver's arrival as starting at 14:13:25 (F5) and treat the gap differently, though the policy measures continuous waiting after the "I'm Here" tap, which was 14:14:10 (F6).
The profile shows the rider already has 1 dispute in 90 d (F16), which the other side may cite to suggest a pattern of fee challenges.

claims.assertion: The driver pressed "I'm Here" at 14:14:10 while the GPS placed him 41 m from the pickup point, within the 200 m arrival radius, so NS-1(i) and (ii) are satisfied.

The rider's own complaint that the driver "cancelled after barely two minutes" corresponds exactly to the recorded timeline: arrival at 14:13:25 and cancellation at 14:15:50, i.e. only 2 min 25 s inside the pickup zone — which is short of the >3 minutes continuous wait required by NS-1(iii).

The wait measured from the "I'm Here" tap to cancellation is even shorter — 1 min 40 s — and the driver's stationary period at the pickup point was 2 min 0 s (14:13:50–14:15:50), so on no reading of the record did the driver wait more than 3 minutes as NS-1(iii) requires.

The "wait >3 min" requirement is not rescued by the driver's message that he was "here at the pickup point" or his post-trip statement that he waited, because system records (F2/F3/F5/F6) contradict those statements and the system records win.
The chat record is complete and fully timestamped (F9, F10, F11), so there is no evidentiary gap and NS-1 can be decided on the record without escalation.

The GPS track covers the whole waiting period — samples at 14:13:25, 14:13:50, 14:14:10, 14:15:35 and cancellation at 14:15:50 — with no gap of more than 2 minutes, so no G12 manual referral is triggered.

The record shows no fee abuse: the driver did push the waiting-button procedure (arrival tap at 41 m) rather than a false arrival press, and he did not charge an additional $5 waiting fee — the only amount on record is the $6.61 cancellation fee (F4, F7).

weaknesses: The driver's own chat message F10 ("3 min up, cancelling the trip") and his written statement F12 assert he had waited three minutes; the rider will use these to argue the threshold was met, and I must concede they sit awkwardly with F5/F6, which measure only 2 min 25 s inside 200 m and 1 min 40 s after the tap.

F17 shows the driver already has one upheld no-show dispute in 90 days; the rider can argue this is a pattern and will press for a flag_account outcome, and while NS-2's flag_account is only triggered when the 200 m arrival test fails (here it passes, F6 — 41 m), the judge may still weigh the profile.

F4 shows the ride was accepted at 14:09:00 and cancelled 6 min 50 s later; the rider may argue the clock should run from acceptance or from first entry into the 200 m zone (14:13:25, F2), and under that reading the wait is not obviously short of three minutes (2 min 25 s is close to the line).

points.response: Accepted as far as it goes: the arrival precondition is met (F6, 41 m). That is exactly why our case turns on the duration limb, which D1 does not touch.
Agreed, and this concedes the decisive point: inside the pickup zone only 2 min 25 s, short of the >3 min continuous wait in NS-1(iii); the fee therefore falls under NS-2.

Agreed — and note the strictest measure, after the driver's own "I'm Here" tap, is only 1 min 40 s (F6), while he told the rider at 14:15 that "3 min" was up (F10); the record refutes him and NS-2 follows.
Agreed: statements F9/F10/F12 lose to system records F2/F3/F5/F6, so nothing on the record establishes three minutes of waiting and the $6.61 cannot stand.
Agreed — the chat is complete and timestamped (F11), so the case can be decided on the record and no G12 referral is needed; deciding it means refund_full under NS-2.
Agreed: samples cover the wait with no gap over 2 minutes (F2, F3, F5, F6), so the 1 min 40 s and 2 min 25 s measurements stand as the true waiting times.

The $5.00 waiting fee is not ours to claim, but this does not save the $6.61 cancellation fee (F7): NS-2 makes the cancellation fee waivable in full whenever NS-1(iii) fails, which D2 and D3 concede it does.

We do not press flag_account: NS-2's account flag applies only where the 200 m arrival test fails, and here the tap was at 41 m (F6); the profile facts (F16, F17) remain context only and do not decide any finding.

Conceded on the precondition only: the driver did tap "I'm Here" at 14:14:10 at 41 m from the pickup (F6), so NS-1(i) and (ii) are met — but that is not the limb in dispute and does not by itself validate or invalidate the fee.

This is the rider's own strongest point and it is correct on every system measure: 1 min 40 s within 200 m after the tap (F6) and 2 min 25 s cumulative before cancellation (F2) both fall short of the >3 minutes of continuous waiting required by NS-1(iii), so the $6.61 fee cannot stand.

Conceded: my chat message at 14:15 claiming "3 min up" (F10) is contradicted by the stationary period of 2 min 0 s at 41 m (F3) and by the tap-to-cancel gap in F6, and under the system-records-win rule that message cannot carry the fee.

Correct — platform arrival was 14:13:25 and cancellation 2 min 25 s later (F5) with no threshold reached, so on NS-2 the $6.61 recorded in F7 must be refunded in full; I withdraw my original request for a refund of that same $6.61 (D1–D7 on the record), which the rider's C2 and C4 now correctly establish.

Conceded, and the concession is drive-only: NS-2 refunds the rider the whole $6.61 because the duration limb failed, but NS-2's extra flag_account is triggered only where the tap was made outside the 200 m radius (m_from_pickup_at_tap > 200), and here the tap was at 41 m (F6), so no fraud flag attaches on that basis.
Conceded: the post-trip statement in F12 is a statement, not a system record, and F5/F6 measure the wait at 1 min 40 s, so it cannot establish the fee.

Void as framed: C7 cites RD-6, which governs account flags for repeated route-deviation breaches, not no-show cases, and this is a no-show dispute with route: 0 in F17; NS-2's flag_account requires the tap to have been made outside the 200 m radius, which F6 shows it was not (41 m), so the profile in F17 cannot support an account-review request here.
